headline: CITED ONLY - introduced in no report
K1-1 medium Every key input breaks the 74HC165's maximum input rise/fall time, by ~16× on press and ~280× on release, and no page says so
K1-10 low SH/LD is described as "falling edge loads"; the load is level-sensitive, and the sample is taken at the rising edge
K1-11 low Bench bring-up leaves SER floating, with no test pad; the README's "only draw is quiescent current" does not hold with a floating CMOS input
K1-12 advisory The key board has no ESD protection, and the main-board TVS does not cover this board's QH
K1-13 advisory No footprint for the damping bulk capacitor that the chain page already expects the key board may need
K1-14 advisory Provenance defects on the threshold and pinout citations
K1-2 medium The page and BOM call the RC a "free hardware debounce", but the switch's banked bounce is 5 ms, 42× longer than the RC's 120 µs window
K1-3 medium key-release-time is restated as "125 µs" on its own owner page and on latency-budget.md ; the value is 119.9 µs, and the checker passes both
K1-4 low key-marker-and-bits.md "Still open" says "the 3 reserved spare-switch positions"; there are 2
K1-5 low "A mid-shift SH/LD reload passes at 11 of 31 reload points" has no derivation and does not reproduce against allocation.yaml
K1-6 low The free-bit pull-up's note says each one "costs the same static draw as a key"; it draws about 1 µA
K1-7 low R-KEY-SER 's stated role ("bounds injected current") is not what it does; it limits C-KEY 's dump into the switch contact, which peaks at 3.3× the KS-33's rating
K1-8 low The 10 kΩ trade is priced as "a 100 µs τ", which is the old 10 kΩ/10 nF network; with the fitted 47 nF it is 470 µs
K1-9 low The pages say the network passives sit "AT the register input, millimetres from the switch"; on the LH board they sit at the switch, up to 44 mm from the register

K2-1 high The rule "an FFSD socket's cable leaves on the side away from its notch" contradicts the banked print. With -RN2 the main-board socket's cable leaves UPWARD, and the drawn route is the one the wrong (standard)
K2-2 medium The closed ribbon's modelled path, and the drc.echo figures derived from it, describe a path the -RN2 cable does not take
K2-3 medium The meter check is scoped to "the first one", but a wrong cable goes in without any mechanical sign, so every cable needs checking before power
K2-4 low The FFSD length field is in inches, while the corpus gives the length in millimetres and says "order that length or the next stock one up"
K2-5 low No check ties the key boards' J-CHAIN pin numbers to the loom netlist's J-CHAIN-KEY- pins; they agree today only by hand
K2-6 low config/body.yaml carries two stale statements about the chain parts
K2-7 advisory The header's 2×6 pad grid is symmetric under a 180° turn, so a hand-fitted J-CHAIN soldered with its mouth backward is electrically 3V3-on-ground
K2-8 advisory hardware/nets.yaml GND_CHAIN.carries gives the grounds as "J-CHAIN pins 1/3/5/7/9" without saying which end
K3-1 medium 20 vias are centred inside SMD or test pads on the reflowed bottom side, and 5 more overlap pads; nothing prevents it
K3-10 advisory PTH and NPTH share one drill file
K3-11 low layout.yaml restates JLC's track/space as 0.127 mm " from memory "; the page banked two lines below says 0.10/0.10
K3-12 advisory ADR 0020's "the PCB carries the ribbon's run as a rule area" is not on the board
K3-13 advisory The register's only label is printed under its own body
K3-2 medium layout.yaml fab: is not what gates the board. Two limits are unchecked, and the rest only warn, which the gate ignores
K3-3 low The silkscreen breaks JLC's legend limits: 0.12 mm and 0.1 mm lines, and silk 0.128 mm and 0.14 mm from pad openings
K3-4 low J-CHAIN : a 0.65 mm finished hole for a 0.41 mm square tail leaves 0.07 mm over the diagonal nominally, and none at JLC's worst-case tolerance
K3-5 low KS-33: a 1.2 mm round hole for a 0.45 × 1.00 mm blade leaves 0.02 mm at worst case, and the banked vendor drawing contradicts itself on the pattern
K3-6 low The router's output is left on its 0.2 mm grid: 449 unmerged collinear fragments, 4 acute junctions, and 180 mm of ground tracks that layout.yaml says are not there
K3-7 low The key-network pad order forces the KEY_LHn node across neighbouring pads, which is where most signal vias come from
K3-8 advisory The decoupling loop closes through the F.Cu plane, 12.9 mm between the capacitor's ground via and pin 8's
K3-9 low The Gerber job file says "Revision": "rev?" ; the board has no title block, and the stackup has no copper weight or mask colour

K4-2 low MECH-KB-STANDOFF names a PEM class with no M2 member
K4-3 low Three of the five bought part numbers have no banked datasheet, and the 74HC165's pin source cites a vendor the board does not buy
K4-4 low The README restates the sheets' part numbers, and already spells one differently
K4-5 low The switches' "MPN" in the hand list is prose, not a part number
K4-6 low The ordering section is not quite enough to place an order
K4-7 advisory SW1-n 's "placed exactly to BOM qty" is a coincidence of two different 2s
K4-8 advisory J-CHAIN's 0.65 mm drill against a 0.41 mm square tail leaves no margin at JLC's lower hole tolerance
K4-9 advisory The U-KEYS row does not carry the fact that makes the vendor matter at 3.3 V

K5-2 medium "Order this length": the FFSD length is overall, outer face to outer face, in inches, ±0.125″ — ordering 86.27 mm leaves up to ~9 mm less free cable than the path needs
K5-3 medium The service position puts the body flat on its bottom face, and the U-bolt stops it: the key plug ends up 11–23 mm lower relative to the main plug than the length assumes
K5-4 low The plate window over J-CHAIN's tails is not needed: the tails stand ~0.95 mm above the board top under a 2.2 mm gap
